name: Motion onset
rule: Each beat has ONE onset, the subject's change (a stroke drawing on, a pop, a tick, a light coming on), started inside the golden box; tier A enters by drawing on, growing or popping (looming); tiers B and C only drift in at a constant speed from an edge or from behind a mass; exits shrink or slide out (they do not capture).
numbers: The onset within ~0.1-0.4 s of a cut, inside x 436-644, y 951-1168 (in the opening it peaks at 0.4-0.7 s); B and C entries >= 370 px (5 degrees) from the focal and never within 0.5 s of A's onset.
evidence: S+, large: onset captures, steady motion and stopping do not; looming captures, receding does not; dynamic features predict saccades up to 3.6x better than static ones
source: attention.md 3 L1 [AT10, AT11, AT12, AT13, AT14, S9]

name: Words
rule: Words live only in the band and in the one number or label per shot; nothing letter-like anywhere else; a caption page is an onset, so the picture's event leads its word.
numbers: >= 56 px for any word in the world; nothing letter-like within 370 px of the focal; the picture leads its caption page by 0.1-0.3 s.
evidence: S+, large: text draws 11.1x and faces 16.6x the fixations of matched regions, even unreadable text
source: attention.md 3 L2 [AT16, AT17, AT21, AT27, AT46]

name: People and animals
rule: A person is the subject or stays tier B (soft, small, steady); the 'you' sits at one side with its head and shoulders turned into the focal's box; strangers stay away from the subject and out of the drop; birds fly straight and even, away from the focal; a face's features only on the beat's subject.
numbers: The 'you' 130-220 px; strangers >= 220 px from the subject's silhouette; features only on figures over ~200 px.
evidence: S+, large: saccades reach faces from 100-110 ms; added people are missed 11 % of the time against 34 % for objects
source: attention.md 3 L3 [AT4, AT16, AT18, AT19, AT20]

name: The screen centre, re-found at every cut
rule: After every cut the focal sits near the visible centre; a focal farther out needs an onset to mark it.
numbers: Within ~150 px (2 degrees) of (540, 960), by default x 410-670, y 950-1050; farther out costs an extra saccade of ~0.2-0.3 s.
evidence: S+, large for the first fixation

name: Value contrast and the brightest area
rule: The hardest value step and the brightest area below the band sit on the subject; no skylit gap, white prop or highlight in the stage outshines the focal's light.
numbers: A step >= 65 L* at the focal; no other light within 10 L* of it.
evidence: S+, medium-large in the first ~0.5 s, small after; our measurement: a brighter patch beat the subject in 12 of 20 reel examples

name: One unique thing in a uniform field (the singleton)
rule: The subject differs from its field in >= 2 channels (value, colour, motion, edge); its field is tone-on-tone with one hot accent only, at the focal; a clear ring round it.
numbers: Within ~370 px of the focal: +-4-6 L*, dE <= 6-8; a clear ring of ~150-220 px round the subject's silhouette.
evidence: S+, large: clutter predicts search time; dense features cut attention and liking (249 ads)
source: attention.md 3 L6 [AT22, AT23, AT24, AT25, AT26, AT28]

name: Words and picture together
rule: The focal sits close under the caption and the picture's event comes just before its word; the caption names what the frame shows.
numbers: The focal 300-450 px under the block (y ~856-1006), 650 px at most; the event 0.1-0.3 s before its word, never after.
evidence: S+, large for learning: temporal contiguity d ~1.22-1.30, spatial d ~0.79-1.10

name: Coherence
rule: Nothing interesting-but-irrelevant: Pip, life and dressing never in the drop, never on a line into the focal, never pulling as hard as half the focal; one idea per shot; no decorative event on a beat that explains.
numbers: Supporting pulls < 50 % of the focal's.
evidence: S+, medium-large: removing extraneous material d ~0.70-0.86; seductive details g ~ -0.33

name: Size
rule: The hook's subject is big, a close is big, and a small subject appears only as the singleton of a calm field, held longer.
numbers: The hook's subject >= 400 px wide (45 % of the visible width); a close >= 650 px; a 130-220 px subject held >= 4 s (est.).

name: A sound on the change
rule: Every onset the viewer must catch gets its own sound, starting with it; supporting life gets a bed, never transient sounds; never a sound on a distractor.
numbers: The sound on the same frame to ~50 ms after the onset (est.).
evidence: S (lab), large in clutter; untested in film

name: Pointers that converge
rule: The vanishing point sits on the subject or behind it; lines end at the focal (they mark the place, they do not carry the eye); people near the story face the subject.
numbers: The vanishing point within 60 px of the subject; lines end within 40 px of the focal's box.
evidence: S for the vanishing point and gaze, 1 for lines; medium; the eye jumps between key elements, it does not ride a line
source: attention.md 3 L11 [AT29, AT20, S9, AT30, AT31]

name: Selective detail
rule: The finest marks and the crisp found edges sit near the focal; lost edges and coarser marks elsewhere.
numbers: Within ~150-300 px of the focal; tier A's small-feature coverage >= 2.5x tier C's (CRAFT.md b).

name: The light as the cue
rule: The story light's pool is on the subject; when the beat changes, the light changes with the event; no arrows, rings or pointing labels.
numbers: The surround 10-20 L* lower than the pool.
evidence: S+, small-medium: cues d ~0.41-0.46; a spotlight cue in an animation helped even what it did not light

name: Emotion
rule: Surprise at the hook, small warm joys in the life, one awe moment, peaks alternating with calm beats; saturation spent only at the focal.
numbers: The hook's surprise at ~2 s; one scale moment a film.

name: Pacing: the event rate
rule: The pace lives in the events, not the cuts: change inside continuous shots; the hook's arousing beat never stacked with fast cuts.
numbers: Caption pages ~1.1-1.5 s; a story event every ~1.5-3 s from the subject's own build; joins >= 3.5 s on average.
source: attention.md 3 L15 [AT43, AT44, AT45, AT46, AT58]

name: One place for both phases
rule: The subject is the frame's salience peak at ~0.3 s (the hardest value step, the brightest area below the band, the beat's one onset, the one hot accent) and its meaning at ~1 s (the thing the caption names).
numbers: Test: at a 1 % squint, flashed for 0.25 s at feed size, the eye lands on the subject.
evidence: S+ [AT5-AT7]; our measurement: the light beat the lines in 12 of 20 reel examples

name: The focal's home, re-found at every cut
rule: By default the focal sits near the visible centre; after a join the new focal sits near the old one or near the centre; anywhere else an onset (motion and sound) marks it in its first 0.3 s.
numbers: Within ~150 px of the centre (x 410-670, y 950-1050); after a join within ~220 px (3 degrees; CRAFT.md a's eye jump <= 0.10 of the diagonal).

name: How big
rule: The hook's and a close's subject are big; a wide's subject takes a share of the height; a small subject appears only as the singleton of a calm field, held long.
numbers: The hook and a close >= 400 px wide (45 % of the visible width); a wide's subject 15-35 % of the frame's height; a subject under ~250 px (3.4 degrees) only in a calm field, held >= 4 s.

name: Against a uniform field, with a clear ring
rule: Near the focal everything but the subject is tone-on-tone; no other named object or crisp detail near the subject's silhouette; the subject differs from its field in >= 2 channels.
numbers: Within ~370 px (5 degrees): +-4-6 L*, dE <= 6-8; the clear ring ~150-220 px (the crowding distance from the words).

name: The subject owns the onsets
rule: In each beat only the subject (or the thread object it hands on) starts, enters, pops, grows or turns; tiers B and C move at a constant speed or not at all, entering only from an edge or from behind a mass.
numbers: First inside the golden box x 436-644, y 951-1168; B and C entries >= 370 px from the focal, never within 0.5 s of A's onset.

name: Persistent changes, spaced events
rule: Every story change leaves its new state on screen; transient events the viewer must catch are spaced; the pieces of one build count as one event.
numbers: The new state >= 0.5 s on screen (better >= 1 s); transient events >= 0.5 s apart (the attentional blink).

name: Words only where they are read
rule: The band, plus one number or label per shot; nothing letter-like anywhere else; the picture's event leads its caption page.
numbers: >= 56 px; nothing letter-like within 370 px of the focal; the lead 0.1-0.3 s, never trailing.

name: People and animals are magnets: give each one a job
rule: A person is the subject or tier B; the 'you' turns its head and shoulders into the focal's box; strangers stay away from the subject and out of the drop; birds and Pip move evenly near the focal; a face's features only on the beat's subject.
numbers: Strangers >= 220 px from the subject's silhouette; no animate turns or flap bursts within 370 px of the focal; features only on figures over ~200 px.

name: Pointers converge on the subject
rule: The vanishing point, every leading line and every sightline end on the subject.
numbers: The vanishing point within 60 px of the subject or behind it; every leading line ends within 40 px of the focal's box; sightlines cross it.

name: Detail where the eye goes
rule: The finest marks and the crisp found edges sit near the focal; lost edges and coarser marks elsewhere.
numbers: Within ~150-300 px of the focal.

name: The light is the cue, and it moves with the event
rule: The story light's pool is on the subject; a light change starts with the event it marks; no arrows, rings or pointing labels.
numbers: The surround 10-20 L* lower than the pool.

name: A sound for each onset that matters
rule: Each onset the viewer must catch has a sound that starts with it; transient sounds only on the subject's events; supporting life is a bed.
numbers: The same frame to ~50 ms after the visual onset.

name: Joins hide on motion and land where the eye is
rule: Cut or carry on the subject's or the carrier's motion; the next focal lands where the eye already is.
numbers: The next focal within ~220 px of the current gaze, or at the centre; nothing new starts in the 0.4 s round the join; a continuity cut on a motion onset goes unseen a third of the time.

name: Event rate, not cut rate
rule: Novelty comes from the subject's own build; no decorative interrupt; the hook's arousing beat never stacked with fast cuts.
numbers: Caption pages ~1.1-1.5 s; a story event every ~1.5-3 s; joins >= 3.5 s on average.

name: The swipe window
rule: The first three seconds follow the eye: words and gist first, then the subject's bold onset, then a second change, then reality overtaking.
numbers: 0-0.4 s the words and the gist (frame 0 being drawn); 0.4-0.7 s the subject's bold onset peaks in the golden box with its sound; 1.2-1.7 s a second change on the subject; ~2 s reality overtakes; one leading pen at <= ~25 px a frame.
evidence: S+ and measured [AT1, AT6, AT12, AT61, V4]

name: The emotional arc
rule: Peaks alternate with calm beats, never a sustained high.
numbers: The hook's surprise at ~2 s; small warm joys in the life; one awe moment (the scale beat).

name: Coherence
rule: Nothing off-story pulls hard, sits in the drop or lies on a line into the focal (Pip's hiding rule is this rule); one idea per shot.
numbers: Off-story pulls < 50 % of the focal's.

name: Measure attention cheaply (tooling)
rule: Check attention with cheap tests rather than by eye alone.
numbers: (a) the flash test: each key frame shown 0.25 s at feed size, 'what is it and where did you look?'; (b) an onset map per 0.5 s window: tier A >= 60 % of the pixels that start moving; (c) a glyph check outside the band; (d) a clutter meter round the focal; spectral-residual saliency is not reliable enough to gate on.

name: Centre-weighted framing: the crop-safe axis
rule: The focal sits on or near the frame's vertical centre line and every key read stays inside the crop-safe stage; off the centre only for a declared reason (a scale shot's landmark, the left-third hero spot, the turn).
numbers: The focal within 130 px of x 540 (x 410-670), y 860-1200; key reads in x 130-870 by y 600-1519 (above y 860 to x 945); for a boosted post above y 1247 and left of x 780 below y 840.
evidence: STUDY for the centre bias [S7, V5]; the crops measured or official; the centring 'trend' ONE SOURCE

name: Stack in depth, move along Z
rule: The near subject low and the far one higher, never side by side at one depth; camera moves in order of preference: push or pull (Z), rise or tilt (Y), truck (X) only when the travel is the story.
numbers: The 'you' 130-220 px with its feet at y ~1220-1510; the subject on the axis at y 950-1200; the far figure 1/2.2-1/3 of the near one's height, tops >= 40 px apart, overlapping >= 10 px or >= 20 px apart.
evidence: CONSENSUS (makers' guides [N38]; micro-drama practice, weaker sources [N39]); STUDY (looming [N11], motion parallax [N12])

name: Height as meaning
rule: Eye level by default; a low angle on the quantity, never on the thing under critique; a high angle once a film on crowds and patterns; overhead only as paper or the 'you's own look down at its hands; no forced three-point perspective.
numbers: As N3 (setups A and B), N11 (horizon y 1114-1229) and N12 (35-55 degrees down).

name: One bold colour, on the subject
rule: One hot accent per scene, at the focal; every other colour tone-on-tone in its mass; the accent travels with the thread object across the joins; never a second saturated patch on the stage.
numbers: Chroma C* >= 50 against tier B's <= 25 (est.); the accent ~3-5 % of the frame (est.); dE <= 6-8 elsewhere.
evidence: STUDY [N13] (the capture is contested); our measurement (reels E8; v6's yellow windows out-shouted the door)

name: The practical as the story light
rule: One story light per scene, on the subject, from a source in the frame whenever the shot allows; glow and bloom at the source only; rims only in the key's colour family; warm practicals against one cool field; no two-colour neon as a default, no volumetric shafts as a show.
numbers: The brightest 5 % below the sky within 134-288 px of the subject; the glow ends >= 10 px outside the band.
evidence: our measurement (reels.md 0); ONE SOURCE each [N29, N30, N33]

name: Drawn depth instead of optical blur
rule: Near and far are separated by drawn cues (the paint coarsens with distance, fewer values, the hue of the air), never by blur, fog or a colour-offset fringe.
numbers: One fixed mix toward the sky per plane (0, 12, 22, 40, 65 %), value steps 5, 5, 4, 3, 2 (CINEMATIC_GUIDE Scale cues 5).
evidence: ONE SOURCE each [N30, N31, N32, N34]; DIRECTION rules 4-5 in force

name: Design complexity up, feature complexity down
rule: A rich arrangement (one device, varied organic silhouettes, 4-6 planes, the far side's density as texture) with little pixel-level clutter away from the focal.
numbers: <= 10 value pieces at a squint; quiet fields within +-4-6 L*; far texture tone-on-tone (+-6 L*); found edges only at the focal; detail peaking just under the horizon and nowhere else.
evidence: STUDY [N16]; STUDY review [N15]; ONE SOURCE blogs [N41]

name: The cut is an attention event: ration it, and make it related
rule: Novelty often, cuts rarely: something new every ~1-2 s from the subject's own build; every join related (carriers A-E); at most 2 plain cuts, each on a 'But'.
numbers: Panels average >= 3.5 s; caption pages every 1.1-1.5 s; F <= 2 a film.
evidence: STUDY [N1, N2, N3, N4]; ONE SOURCE official [N25]

name: Motivated moves: a push is looming; a pull needs its own event
rule: Every camera move has a story reason: the push says 'this matters', the pull 'see where it sits'; a pull-out carries its own attention event; no zoom in a hold.
numbers: A story push >= 3 % in <= 2 s, <= 2x per panel, on its word, the picture ~0.1 s ahead of the voice.
evidence: STUDY (looming captures, receding does not [N11]); MEASURED (Arcane, research/cine_motion.md 1)

name: Asymmetric easing: decelerate in, accelerate out, move on arcs
rule: Things that arrive decelerate, things that leave accelerate, travellers move on arcs; position and scale only, never opacity.
numbers: Arrivals over 0.25-0.45 s (15-27 f; decelerate cubic-bezier(0.05, 0.7, 0.1, 1.0)); exits over 0.15-0.25 s (9-15 f; accelerate cubic-bezier(0.3, 0.0, 0.8, 0.15)); the thread on an arc or an S, never a ruler line.
evidence: ONE SOURCE official [N24]; MEASURED (Arcane); CONSENSUS (animation principles [S5])

name: Stepped drawings, smooth camera
rule: Drawn poses and drawn effects step while the camera, the parallax, the light and the captions move on every frame.
numbers: A pose held ~5 f at 60 fps ('twos' at 24 fps = 83 ms; 'threes' 7-8 f).
evidence: ONE SOURCE each [N30, N32]; DIRECTION rule 8 in force

name: 2.5D inside its limits: the hole rule
rule: Painted planes moved by one camera hold only within a range: a move uncovers a strip between neighbouring planes, so the farther plane is painted past the nearer one's edge; every plane carries its own perspective.
numbers: The farther plane painted >= its relative shift + 40 px (the float's overscan) behind the nearer one's edge; Z moves uncover least, sideways most (a truck's background = the view plus the travel); 4-6 planes, 5-7 on a vista; the nearest plane moves only inside its overscan.

name: Sideways motion reads faster in 9:16
rule: For the same felt calm, sideways movers and moves go about half as fast per frame as vertical ones; travel by tilt or rise where the story allows.
numbers: The visible width 884 px against the height 1920: a mover crosses the width 2.2x sooner (est.).

name: Eye trace: the attended thing keeps its screen spot across the join
rule: Across a cut or a transition, the thing the eye is on (or the next shot's subject) sits where the eye already is.
numbers: The next focal within 150 px (2 degrees) of the last; within 370 px (5 degrees) one short saccade (~0.2 s); 190 px for a light match; beyond that only where a carrier leads or on an F cut.

name: Sound leads the cut
rule: The next shot's sound (for us the voice's next sentence) starts at or just before the picture changes.
numbers: A join's midpoint on the next sentence's first word; the picture ~0.1 s ahead of its word; a join never in a pause of the voice longer than ~0.3 s (est.).

name: Coherence: no seductive detail
rule: Everything in the frame serves the beat; interesting but irrelevant extras are cut.
numbers: <= 6 named objects (the subject, the thread, one big quiet mass, 1-3 supporting things); Pip >= 250 px from the focal, off the eye path; no joke props, no logos, no readable fine print.

name: Signalling: one highlight, on its word
rule: The essential is cued at the moment it is said, one signal at a time; all of a beat's signals land on the same word.
numbers: The caption's keyword, the light's peak, the accent's arrival and the push on one word; the picture ~0.1 s ahead; no arrows or callout boxes.
evidence: META [N19]: retention g = 0.53, transfer g = 0.33; STUDY [N20]

name: The live drawing, with a visible agent
rule: The picture is drawn while you watch, the drawer's tool (our pen tip) in view.
numbers: Frame 0's draw-on: a moving pen tip at full contrast, the line the darkest mark, >= 1 s, peaking after 0.4 s; after frame 0 only where the drawing is the beat, the tip in view.
evidence: STUDY [N20] (hand in view d = 0.35, no hand d = -0.16), [N21]

name: Congruence and apprehension: animate the real mechanism, slowly enough to see
rule: The motion shows the structure of what it explains (cause, then effect, one tick per unit) at a speed the eye can follow.
numbers: Each unit of cause one visible tick of the effect; each step held ~0.4 s or more unless one of many read as a flow (est.); one causal chain at a time.

name: Words few and big, in one home
rule: On-screen words are few, large, in one fixed place, in step with the voice.
numbers: Captions only in the band (98 px, <= 2 lines, lines <= 780 px), popping in place on the voice; at most one label or number in the world (>= 56 px; a number 120-160 px); no title over the picture; no kinetic type through the stage.

name: One story motion at a time
rule: Either the camera moves and the subject is the still pivot, or the camera holds and the subject moves; never both freely; the world's life slow, even, low in contrast, taking turns.
numbers: The pivot within +-40 px; <= 3-4 noticeable movers; none entering in the 0.4 s round a join.

name: A move is three designed frames
rule: The start, middle and end frames each pass the composition rules as stills; the caption band is a fixed mat at every frame; anything crossing the band during a move is flat or in the gutters.
numbers: Three frames: p 0, 0.5, 1; the band one flat field throughout; plane edges across it only at x < 95 or > 945.

name: Pick the move and the join from the composition's device
rule: An opening -> the push-through; one shape or light at one spot -> a match; lines into depth -> the subject travels or a push; a tall thing -> a tilt; two levels -> a crane or a tilt; a near layer -> the float and the wipe; negative space -> a hold or the float, never a push; a pattern's break -> the build or the light pull.
numbers: (see each device's pairs_with)
evidence: our analysis of the owner's 41 in motion (motion.md 2)

name: The default motion is the owner's E9
rule: The camera holds while the subject travels the device's line at its scale's speed, its onset on its word, crossing an OPENING or entering or leaving, never the whole frame.
numbers: ~0.8 x its height in px per second; an opening crossed in ~1-2 s.

name: The float
rule: The parallax float as in force, by depth, home by every join; in a mirrored frame its legs run vertical only.
numbers: 8-15 px/s at the near plane, peak <= 25 px/s, net within +-12 px of home.
evidence: MEASURED (COZY_AND_SCALE 3b.5: the cozy reference's float 10.1 px/s); est. for the mirror

name: The story push
rule: A push is a story move: visible, bounded, about its target, one per beat, on its word; a lean-in lands on a settle, a drawn-in push peaks late.
numbers: >= 3 % per 2 s; <= 2x per panel; scaled about the target's centre; a drawn-in push peaks at 65-80 % of its length.

name: A pull carries its own event
rule: A pull-out reveal is used only with its own attention event (a light burst, the landmark rising on its word, birds crossing toward it).
numbers: The event before the landing (S5: the light burst at p 0.5-0.55, the landmark lands by p 0.96).

name: Reveal tilts
rule: A vertical reveal is slow and front-loaded, a pan-head shift with no zoom-out.
numbers: 600-900 px in 3.5-4.5 s, front-loaded (unveil = trapezoid(0.1, 0.6)) or linear.
evidence: MEASURED (Arcane: all 7 vertical reveals peak at <= 45 %)

name: Sideways is expensive in 9:16
rule: Prefer the tilt, the push and the pull; a sideways pan of a detailed frame stays slow; a sideways mover goes at about half the px per frame of a vertical one.
numbers: A full-frame sideways pan of detail <= ~6 px/f (est., to test; the 7-second rule at 60 fps).

name: Easing
rule: Arrivals decelerate, exits accelerate, camera moves ease in AND out, long moves cruise, a join's two legs meet at one velocity; never a linear camera start or stop, never a camera bounce, never staggered starts across many movers.
numbers: Arrivals over 15-27 f, exits over 9-15 f; the cruise trapezoid(0.25, 0.35) peaks at 1.43x the mean.

name: The light pull is our focus pull
rule: The new focal takes the hardest step while the old one drops; one light change at a time, with something new at the new focal; never more than 3 flashes a second.
numbers: The new focal >= 65 L*, the old one down >= 10-15 L*; a lamp 0.1-0.3 s, the sky ~1 s; >= 0.5 s from any other onset.

name: Choose the join by what changes
rule: Closer or wider in one place -> the continuous camera; into a place seen through an opening -> the push-through; to another place with the thread -> a shape or light match; following a traveller -> the carry; a jump that must not show -> the wipe; one thing becomes another -> the morph; time passes -> the light change; to the proof -> the card flip; the turn -> the plain cut; the end -> the loop.
numbers: motion.md 4.3's table: <= 1.15x or 150 px over 1.4 s (C); the opening 15-30 %, 1.1 s (A); the anchor within 150 px (190 for a light) and 1.5x (B); the same speed and direction (D carry); >= 70 % of the stage covered (D wipe); 0.4-0.8 s (morph); a lamp 0.1-0.3 s, the sky 0.4-1.5 s; at most 2 F.

name: Join numbers
rule: The next focal stays near the last; the push-through's opening is big enough and shown long enough; a match keeps its anchor's spot and size; ONE change across a match.
numbers: The next focal within 150 px of the last (370 px at most) except on F; J2's opening 15-30 % of the frame, shown >= 0.5 s, a flat light field before the zoom passes ~3 % a frame; J3's anchor within 150 px and 1.5x (1.2x for the thread itself); J4's light within 190 px.
evidence: modern.md M19-M21; MEASURED (Arcane T1, T7); est.

name: The cut on action
rule: The motion runs on after the cut in the same screen direction; it counts as an F unless the thread crosses the cut.
numbers: The motion >= 0.3 s after the cut.

name: The carry
rule: The traveller keeps its speed and direction across the cut; vertical carries suit 9:16.
numbers: The same speed within ~10 %; it enters within 0-2 f.

name: The wipe
rule: The wiper is a tier-C near mass already in the outgoing shot, our own organic shape in the clean pen, never a stranger's back; once or twice a film.
numbers: >= 70 % of the stage covered on the cut frame, <= 0.5 s on screen, its own 8-12 f window.
evidence: STUDY [MO23]; MEASURED (Arcane T5, S5); DIRECTION rules 3-4

name: The morph
rule: Staged (position, then shape and colour, then the world); the object the brightest and hottest thing throughout; never two in a row.

name: Time passes by light, in place
rule: A lamp, the sky's moving edge, a cloud; the dissolve stays a declared exception.
numbers: A lamp 0.1-0.3 s; the sky ~0.8-1.5 s for 'time passes' (est.).

name: No whip
rule: If one is ever declared: the same direction and speed on both sides, one smear drawing, no blur.
numbers: ~0.33 s; the smear held 2-3 f.

name: Sound across a join
rule: The picture leads its word; a place's ambience may lead its picture and trail under the next, ducked; one bridge per join; an effect sits on its event or just after.
numbers: The picture 0.1-0.3 s ahead of its word; ambience leads 0.2-0.5 s, trails 0.3-1.0 s; an effect on its event's frame or 1-2 f after, never > 2 f before (detected from +45 ms lead or 125 ms lag).

name: Joins sit at the breakpoint
rule: A join sits at the end of a sentence or an action, where viewers blink; its midpoint on the next sentence's first word; never mid-action except a cut on action; never a cut in the middle of a move.
numbers: The midpoint on the next sentence's first word (in force).

name: Life's speed by its scale
rule: A walker moves at ~0.8 x its height in px per second; huge means slow; the near mover is the fastest.
numbers: Far walkers 15-60 px tall ~12-50 px/s; mid walkers 110-260 px ~90-215 px/s; the 180 px 'you' ~150 px/s; clouds 0-15 px/s.

name: The build
rule: One pen tip leads; the opening's draw-on is long enough to see after the swipe; pieces of one build come fast, separate reads slowly.
numbers: The tip at ~12-25 px/f; the draw-on >= 1 s, peaking after 0.4 s; one build's pieces every 0.1-0.2 s (in seconds, not frames); separate reads >= 0.5 s apart.

name: Check it
rule: Every move and join is checked by tools: on-screen speed (with a lateral warning), dead frames, the gate's join counts, and the new join checks.
numbers: scripts/camspeed.py (+ a lateral WARN ~6 px/f), scripts/qa/deadframes.py, scripts/qa/gate_check.py, the carry and eye-jump tool promoted from the retro tools, the anchor / carry / aperture / sound-offset checks.

name: Design for the window the phone shows
rule: Key reads sit inside the clear window; only masses run into the cut strips, under the rails and under the bottom UI; a thing cut by a side edge must still read with its outer 98 px gone.
numbers: Key reads in x 130-945 from y 600 to 860 and x 130-870 from y 860 to 1519; nothing to read above y 240 or at y >= 1519; words >= 56 px (the fluent floor is a 17 px x-height), lines >= 2 px, a figure 'doing what' >= 40 px and reliably 60-80 px.

name: Three stacked pictures
rule: The words' sky (the band one flat field, nothing across it), the stage (the story) and the near band (one quiet mass under the app's text); depth stacks up the frame; one stage, never a split screen.
numbers: y 0-600 / 600-1520 / 1250-1920; planes overlap >= ~10 px, no two plane tops within ~40 px; width is 884 visible px.
evidence: our measurement (16 of the reels' 21 focal points land in or within 40 px of R7's box); cinema.md 1, 4.8; vertical.md 2

name: One focal, in its home
rule: The focal's centre sits on the subject axis, by default near x 540 and close under the captions; off its home only for a declared reason; nothing calls in the drop.
numbers: x 380-700 (by default x 410-670), y 860-1200, default spot y 950-1050; the drop from the block's foot (y 556) 300-650 px (4-8.7 degrees), the short end (300-450 px) whenever the shot allows.
evidence: STUDY (the centre bias [S7], [V5]); R7; C1; V8

name: The focal is one place: the subject, the story light and the hardest value step
rule: The subject, the brightest light and the hardest step coincide; the one hot accent only there; the lines lead, the light decides.
numbers: A step >= 65 L* at the focal; below the band no other step over ~40 L* and no light within 10 L* of the focal's; the brightest 5 % below the sky within 134-288 px (0.07-0.15 H) of the subject; dE <= 6-8 elsewhere; <= 3 regions pull at >= 50 % of the strongest and only one at >= 70 %.
evidence: our measurement (reels.md 0, 6: the light beat the lines in 12 of 20); in force as DIRECTION rules 2 and 5 and the playbook's PROPER LIGHT

name: Notan first: three masses, two quiet fields
rule: Draw the 3-value notan of every shot before anything else: three big masses, two connected quiet fields, the things living in the belt between.
numbers: At a 1 % squint in 3 values the three largest masses >= 85 % (<= 8 masses >= 1 %), one value group 40-55 %, the means >= 13 L* apart; <= 10 value pieces; <= 6 named objects; >= 65 % quiet in two fields (the sky with the band >= 30 %, the near ground >= 15 %), each patterned within +-4-6 L*; Pip >= 250 px from the focal.
evidence: our measurement of the owner's references (organic/composition.md 1-2); in force as DIRECTION rules 2-3
source: COMPOSITION_SHOTS.md 1 rule 5 (R1, R2, R5, R6, R10, R12)

name: The horizon off the half, declared per set
rule: Each set declares setup A or B with its camera height and keeps it in every shot; thirds as proportions, never two equal halves of anything.
evidence: Smith 1797 via [S3]; the owner's references put the horizon at 0.57-0.85 H

name: People stand by the horizon-cut rule; the 'you' is soft, at one side, looking in
rule: Every standing figure is placed by the horizon-cut formula; the 'you' is one soft figure at one side, its sightline into the focal's box; strangers small and in groups.
numbers: Feet at y_h + P*c/h, head at y_h - P*(h - c)/h; the 'you' 130-220 px, tier B (pull < 50 %), x 130-380 facing right or x 700-830 facing left, its head top above y ~1380; lead room 1.5-2x; mid walkers 110-260 px, far 15-60 px, in twos and threes.
evidence: cinema.md 3.2, C9; our measurement (the reels' figures: 8 of 12 at 150-226 px)

name: One device per shot, and it delivers the eye to the focal
rule: Name one device by its code; a second only when it points at the same focal; lines lead to the focal and stop there.
numbers: Lines in 2-3 legs of >= 150 px alternating sides at ~40-60 degrees, the last leg within 40 px of the focal's box; no line corner to corner, across the band or into an empty vanishing point; the vanishing point within 60 px of the subject; an inner frame 15-30 %, its aperture >= 10 L* off its rim; a pattern within +-6 L* with one break.
evidence: CONSENSUS (Smith, Dow, Poore, staging: C6, C7, C14); the reels teach one device per example

name: One soft counterweight, high or on the far side
rule: The near-centre focal is balanced by one big soft mass far out on the other side, never in the lower right where the app already weighs; the words on top balanced by the near dark mass.
numbers: The focal 0-130 px off x 540; the counterweight >= 300 px out (x < 240 or > 840), bigger and softer, pull < 50 %; by default the hero cloud in the top gutter (y 0-290); never at x > 830 below y 790.
evidence: CONSENSUS (the steelyard: Poore 1903, Payne 1941, via cinema.md S1); C8, R8, V11

name: The near frame is a hint at the edges
rule: Things are cut by the frame's edges; the near frame holds a few props inside its shade mass; one framing mass on one side; found edges only at the focal; no tangents.
numbers: >= 2 things cut by the edges in every shot; the near frame <= 2 props within 8 L* of its shade mass; a framing mass on one side only, <= 216 px; never half the frame, never a blur; contours overlap >= ~10 px or keep >= ~20 px apart.
evidence: the owner's words (the playbook: 'a small, subtle hint at the edges'); R6, R9, C13

name: Sizes step 2-3x; an angle means something
rule: Sizes are set on the beat's subject and step 2-3x; a plain cut changes size or angle enough to read as meant; eye level by default, other angles only for their meaning.
numbers: Extreme wide ('you' 60-150 px), wide (the subject 15-35 % of the height), medium (270-460 px wide), close (>= 650 px), insert; a push <= 2x per panel; a plain cut >= 20 % in size (G3_ANIMATIC, in force; this library asks 1.5-2x) or >= 30 degrees, or the exact frame; low only on the quantity; high once, on crowds; overhead only as paper; no roll.

name: A move is three designed frames, and the subject is its pivot
rule: The start, middle and end frames each pass the rules; one variable per move on one ease; the subject holds its spot or travels one path; holds are locked or float; one speed budget.
numbers: The middle (p 0.5) passes at least the band and tangent checks; the subject within +-40 px or on one path between two golden-box points; holds locked or the float at 8-15 px/s; ~15 px per frame at 60 fps.
evidence: C12; DIRECTION rule 8; CINEMATIC_GUIDE rules 1-3; our measurement (17 of 23 reel shots locked or nearly)

name: Frame 0 peaks after the swipe settles
rule: The opening's bold event runs long enough and peaks after the page settles; one gist at a quarter second.
numbers: The page settles in ~0.4 s (half its travel in 0.07 s); the event >= 1 s with its biggest change after 0.4 s; one subject on the axis >= 400 px wide with the hardest step; the first spoken line in the band from frame 0; nothing important in the bottom 400 px or the outer 98 px.
evidence: MEASURED (the swipe on the owner's phone, vertical.md 4); V9

name: The focal's home
rule: The beat's focal sits in the stage square's golden box; off it only for a declared reason (a left-third spiral, a scale shot, a chart).
evidence: STUDY (the centre bias [S7, S10]); R7's drop

name: The horizon
rule: The horizon sits near a third or a golden line of the full frame, never near the half; breathers and scale shots keep CINEMATIC_GUIDE's numbers.
numbers: y 640-860 (setup B) or 1150-1300 (setup A); never y 900-1020.

name: The camera height, per set
rule: W1 declares the setup per set; every standing figure is placed by the horizon-cut rule.
numbers: A: 0.9-1.6 m, horizon 0.60-0.68 H; B: 3-7 m, horizon 0.36-0.45 H; feet y_h + P*c/h, head y_h - P*(h - c)/h.
evidence: the owner's references (horizon 0.57-0.85 H); CRAFT.md f.5

name: The size ladder
rule: Sizes step 2-3x; a plain cut between two shots of one subject changes size or angle enough, or keeps the exact frame.
numbers: An F cut >= ~1.5-2x in size or >= 30 degrees in angle.

name: Angles
rule: Eye level is the default; a low angle only on the quantity; a high angle only on crowds, patterns and maps; overhead only as paper; never a Dutch tilt.

name: One device per shot
rule: One device does the leading, pointing at the focal; a second only when it points at the same focal; the G3 panel names it.
numbers: (see CS8)
evidence: Smith, Dow, Poore, staging [S1-S3, S5, S6]

name: The eye's path
rule: The path enters from the near band or the words, zigzags in a few legs and ends on the focal; never straight out.
numbers: 2-3 zigzag legs of >= 150 px; the last leg within 40 px of the focal's box; no line corner to corner, none through the band; no empty vanishing point behind the focal.
evidence: Poore's entrance and exit [S1]; layout pathways [S16]

name: The steelyard
rule: The near-centre focal is balanced by one far, bigger, softer counterweight; the words on top balanced by the near dark mass.
numbers: The focal <= 130 px off x 540; the counterweight >= 300 px out on the other side, < 50 % of the focal's pull, never isolated and crisp.

name: Facing and lead room
rule: A facing or moving subject gets more room in front; the 'you' beside the subject stands outside the axis on the side it looks from, facing in.
numbers: 1.5-2x room in front (facing right at x 380-430, facing left at 650-700); the 'you' at x 120-380 or 700-900, its sightline through the focal's box.
evidence: lead room [S14]; the inward bias [S10]; gaze cues [S9]

name: The G3 panel is a layout
rule: Each panel declares what a 2D layout holds.
numbers: Eight declarations: size and setup; vanishing point, device and path; focal box and counterweight; planes (4-6, each top's y and float factor); a 3-value notan; the 'you' and Pip; the move's three frames; the hook-up.

name: The value script and the colour script
rule: One strip per film plans the intensity curve in value, then colour; the key changes only on a story turn, carried by light.
numbers: One 108 x 192 px thumbnail per beat (~8-14 a film), values at W1/G3, colour at G4; affinity in cozy beats, contrast at the hook, the turn and the payoff; an ordinary join keeps the colour shift <= 15.

name: Moves
rule: A camera move is a sequence of compositions: three designed frames, one variable, the subject the pivot, lead room growing, the band a fixed mat, tangents passing quickly.
numbers: Start, middle, end; the pivot +-40 px or one path between two golden points; a push scales about the target's centre; tangents pass in <= ~0.1 s.

name: Staging
rule: An action reads in silhouette; one actor at a time; overlap or air, never a kiss; the background read in a glance.
numbers: The silhouette test at 0.25 scale (270 px wide); action in profile or 3/4 back, the acting part >= ~12 px outside the body; contours overlap >= ~10 px or keep >= ~20 px apart; the background gets ~0.25 s of a 3.5 s shot.

name: Rhythm and symmetry
rule: A repeated motif is one texture with one break, the break being the call; full symmetry is rare; never two equal halves of anything.
numbers: Full symmetry in at most two shots a film, for formal beats.

name: Design to the feed's visible frame
rule: On the owner's feed only the middle of the frame's width is seen: key reads stay inside it, and anything cut by the edge must still read.
numbers: Visible x 98-982 (52 px a side on a profile, up to 108 on 20:9 phones); key reads inside x 130-945.

name: The rails, measured
rule: Nothing to read under the right rails.
numbers: x > 945 from y 790 (TikTok x 948-1059 from y 797) and x > 870 from y 860 (Instagram's Reels tab x 877-954 from y 1032, ~860 with a repost button), down to y 1520.

name: The top, measured
rule: Nothing to read under the header and its scrim.
numbers: Above y 240 (the header to y 218-235, a 10 % scrim to ~240); the band from y 290 stays.

name: The bottom, measured
rule: Under the app's text, one quiet dark-mid mass with no light detail and no call.
numbers: The app's text from y 1519; the scrim darkens the bottom a further 10-20 %.

name: Caption lines <= 780 px
rule: Caption lines stay short enough for every crop.
numbers: Lines <= 780 px (x 130-910 on the x 520 centre line, ~23 characters at 98 px), <= 2 lines.

name: Caption pace
rule: A page stays long enough to read.
numbers: A page's characters <= 20 x its seconds on screen.

name: Sizes by angle
rule: Words, lines and cover titles are sized by the angle they make on the phone.
numbers: A word's x-height >= 0.2 degrees on the feed (>= 17 px; our 56 px floor keeps 1.5x over it); lines >= 2 px; a cover title meant for a grid tile ~115-130 px.

name: The centre column and the focal's home
rule: Key reads in the centre column; the focal centred in the visible stage's golden box, a short drop under the words.
numbers: Key reads x 130-945 from the band to y 860 and x 130-870 from y 860 to 1519; the focal in x 436-644, y 951-1168; the drop 300-450 px preferred, 650 at most.

name: Frame 0 in the swipe
rule: The opening's bold event lasts long enough and peaks after the page settles.
numbers: The event >= 1 s, peaking after 0.4 s; the subject (tier A) >= 400 px wide on the axis with the hardest value step; the first spoken line in the band from frame 0.

name: One stage, no split screens
rule: A comparison is a sequence, or one frame with the subject at the seam.
numbers: (one stage under the band)

name: The interface is in the picture
rule: Our own pulls stay out of the interface's way; leading lines never end at the name block.
numbers: No call of ours at x > 830 below y 790 or below y 1480; the counterweight high or left.

name: Review as the feed shows it
rule: Every review is also checked at the Reels tab's crop and scale with its interface drawn over it.
numbers: Visible x 98-982, our frame 1.22x its fit-to-screen size.

name: Reference sizes through the feed
rule: A landscape reference shown at full phone width maps its width to 883 of our px on the owner's feed, not 1080.
numbers: x 0.82 for what the owner sees.

name: Ads
rule: Key reads stay inside the intersection of the platforms' official safe areas.

name: Design the notan first
rule: Three value masses hold most of the frame; one value group dominates; the groups are well apart; a notan of every exterior shot at G3.
numbers: At a 1 % squint in 3 values the three masses >= 85 % (<= 8 masses >= 1 %); one group 40-55 %; the means >= 13 L* apart.

name: Few pieces
rule: Few value pieces; the rest is texture inside a mass.
numbers: <= 10 value pieces (0.02-1 % of the frame each); variation within a mass 2-8 L*.

name: One call
rule: Few regions pull, and only the focal pulls hard, in value and in colour.
numbers: <= 3 regions at >= 50 % of the strongest, only one at >= 70 %.
evidence: our measurement (the painted models 1-2 calls; v6 10); staging (Thomas and Johnston 1981)

name: The focal is the subject, the story light and the frame's hardest value step
rule: Counterchange at the one spot: light against dark.
numbers: A step >= 65 L* (the lit doorway L* >= 95, her silhouette <= 28); below the band no other step over ~40 L*, nothing within 10 L* of the door's light; the brightest 5 % below the sky within 0.07-0.15 H of her.

name: Big quiet
rule: Most of the frame is quiet at a squint, in two connected masses; quiet is never empty.
numbers: >= 65 % quiet: the sky field >= 30 % (the band inside it) and the near ground >= 15 %, each patterned within +-4-6 L*.

name: How many props
rule: Few named objects; the near frame a hint; the far side full as texture.
numbers: <= 6 named objects at phone size; the near frame <= 2 props, cut by an edge, within 8 L* of the near shade mass; far density within +-6 L* of its band.
evidence: our measurement (the references 4-6; v6 ~40); the owner's words (2026-10-29)

name: The caption band sits in the light quiet mass, and the focal sits just under it
rule: The eye reads the words, then drops once, a short way, to the light; nothing calls between.
numbers: The band y 290-600 flat (dL* <= 1.5, ink >= 7:1); the focal's centre y 860-1200, x 380-700, <= 0.2 W off x 520, 300-650 px below y 556; the glow stops >= 10 px outside the band.
evidence: LAYOUT's read zone; our reading of the city posters

name: One counterweight
rule: One big, soft, quiet secondary mass balances the small loud focal from the other side.
numbers: The hero cloud in the top gutter (y 0-290) and the side gutter (x > 945), pull < 50 % of the focal's, its lit side toward the key.

name: Edges: found at the focal, lost elsewhere
rule: The crispest edges and the hardest step only at the focal; where two masses are close in value the edge goes soft or lost.
numbers: Edges 0.5-1.5 px at the focal; lost wherever two masses sit within ~10 L*.
evidence: PAINT_RECIPES.md 1.6; the playbook (edges lost and found)

name: A real dark mass
rule: The darkest value group is a real, connected mass below the band.
numbers: 15-40 % of the frame, mean L* <= 45, >= 80 % of it in one or two connected masses below the band.

name: Colour follows the value plan
rule: The hot accent only at the focal; everything else tone-on-tone inside its mass.
numbers: dE <= 6-8 elsewhere; far lit windows +6-8 L* inside the facade's mass, never a saturated yellow unless one is the subject.
evidence: our measurement (v6's yellow windows were the colour's strongest call)

name: Pip and the eye path
rule: Pip hides tone-on-tone inside a mass of the busy belt, off the eye path.
numbers: >= 250 px from the focal; never between the words and the focal or on a leading line into it.
evidence: the playbook (Pip); our analysis of v6
